slides.heading: Reception — Spring 1, Week 3
slides.sub: New sounds taught directly, practised and applied in words, captions and the matching decodable book.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "sh" (/ʃ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="ship" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="ship"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Shelly the snail slides into her shell and whispers shhh when the garden gets too noisy.

character.name: Shelly
character.blurb: Shelly is a shy snail who tucks into her shell and hushes everyone with a soft shhh.

slides.pronunciation_note: A soft, quiet sound you can hold, 'shhh' — like asking for quiet, no vowel added on the end.
slides.formation_cue: Write 's', then 'h', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Hold one finger up to your lips and whisper shhh.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="ship" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="ship"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.tip: Another short word where 'e' says its name 'ee' — notice it rhymes with he, she, we and me, so they're easy to spot as a family.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "th" (/θ/, /ð/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="thumb" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="thumb"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Theo the tortoise pokes his tongue out just a little, th-th, whenever he's thinking hard.

character.name: Theo
character.blurb: Theo isn't a tortoise but a slow, thoughtful mushroom who pokes a little tongue-shaped frill out when he's puzzling something over.

slides.pronunciation_note: Pop your tongue tip gently between your teeth and blow, 'th' — it can sound soft (thin) or buzzy (that), practise both.
slides.formation_cue: Write 't', then 'h', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Poke your tongue tip gently between your teeth and blow softly, th-th.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="thumb" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="thumb"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ng" (/ŋ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="ring" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="ring"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Nigel the nest hums a long, low ng-ng note that wobbles the twigs around him.

character.name: Nigel
character.blurb: Nigel is a cosy nest that hums a low ng note whenever the wind rocks him gently.

slides.pronunciation_note: A hum made at the back of the mouth, 'ng' — like the end of 'sing', hold it and feel your nose buzz slightly.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'n', then 'g', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Hum ng-ng with your mouth slightly open and the back of your tongue raised, and tap your nose gently to feel it buzz.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="ring" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="ring"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.

slides.dictation: A thing is in the bag.
